newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CURLING-CANADA AND NORWAY TO MEET IN CURLING CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: CURLING-CANADA AND NORWAY TO MEET IN CURLING CLASSIC.

text.p: Canada's Sandra Schmirler and Norway's Dordi Nordby posted semifinal wins at the world curling championships on Friday to set up a historic showdown.
The final on Saturday will be a battle between the only two women to skip rinks to back-to-back championships, the winner becoming the first to claim three titles.
The two women have dominated their sport in the 90s, Nordby claiming gold in 1990 and 1991 with Schmirler leading Canada to titles in 1993 and 1994.
Canada advanced with a 5-2 win over Denmark while Norway blasted Japan 12-5.
The men's semifinals featured a pair of upsets.

Kevin Martin's Edmonton rink, looking to give Canada a fifth consecutive title, were surprised 6-4 by Sweden's Peter Lindholm. The other semifinal saw German veteran Andy Kapp dispose of Scotland's Hammy McMillen 6-3.
The two winners will automatically become gold medal favourites at the Nagano Olympics where curling will be a full medal sport for the first time.
